title: Longest Common Prefix
description: Given a list of strings `strs`, return the longest string that every element starts with. If the strings share no leading characters, return the empty string `""`.

examples.explanation: All three begin with fl; the third letter differs (o vs i).
An empty string is a member, so the common prefix is empty.

constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters
hints: The answer can never be longer than the shortest string.
Compare column by column: look at character 0 of every string, then character 1, and stop at the first column that is not uniform.
Python's zip(*strs) yields exactly those columns and stops at the shortest string for free.
approach:
**Key insight: scan vertically.** Look at position 0 of every string, then position 1, and so on. The first position where the strings disagree, or where the shortest string runs out, ends the prefix. `zip(*strs)` produces exactly these columns and stops at the shortest string, so if no column disagrees the whole shortest string is the answer.

The horizontal alternative (take `strs[0]`, shrink it until every string starts with it) is also O(S) where S is the total number of characters, but vertical scanning exits early on inputs like `["a"*1000, "b"*1000]`.

**Common mistakes:** indexing past the end of a short string; returning `strs[0]` when the list has one element without handling the general case; sorting and comparing only first and last string (works, but O(n log n) and harder to justify).

**Interview follow-ups:** Many queries against a fixed dictionary? Build a trie; the common prefix of the whole set is the path from the root while each node has exactly one child and is not a word end. Longest common prefix of two arbitrary strings among the set (pairwise LCP queries)? Sort the strings; the LCP of any two is the minimum LCP of adjacent pairs between them, answerable with a sparse table. Divide and conquer is a natural parallel version.

complexity.time: O(S) where S is the total number of characters
